Yes. `find_logs` (line 12) filters with `p.is_file()`, which follows the symlink and returns `True` for a link to a regular file, so a matching symlink enters the rotation set.

Two related notes on that path:
- `compress` reads through the link. It then calls `path.unlink()`, which removes the link only. The link target stays on disk.
- `prune_archives` (line 28) does not filter by `is_file()` at all, so it can `unlink()` a `.gz` symlink or any other `.gz` entry.
